[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Attention Mechanisms and Bahdanau/Luong Attention in NLP"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Attention mechanisms have revolutionized Natural Language Processing (NLP) by addressing the information bottleneck inherent in traditional Encoder-Decoder architectures, particularly in tasks like Neural Machine Translation (NMT)."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"The Encoder-Decoder Bottleneck Problem"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"In standard seq2seq models, the encoder compresses the entire input sequence into a single fixed-length context vector. As the input sentence grows longer, the model struggles to retain all relevant information, leading to poor performance on long sequences."},{"order":5,"type":"heading","text":"Introduction to Attention"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"The attention mechanism solves this bottleneck by allowing the decoder to look back at all encoder hidden states at every decoding step. Instead of relying on a single vector, the model computes a weighted sum of encoder outputs, dynamically focusing on the most relevant parts of the input."},{"order":7,"type":"heading","text":"Bahdanau Attention (Additive Attention)"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Introduced by Dzmitry Bahdanau et al. in 2014, Additive Attention computes the alignment score using a single hidden layer feed-forward network. It uses the previous decoder hidden state and the current encoder hidden state."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Score function: e_ij = v_a^T * tanh(W_a * s_{i-1} + U_a * h_j)"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Weights are computed using a softmax function over the alignment scores."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Context vector is the weighted sum of all encoder hidden states."},{"order":12,"type":"heading","text":"Luong Attention (Multiplicative Attention)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Proposed by Minh-Thang Luong et al. in 2015, Multiplicative (or Dot-Product) Attention simplifies the scoring function and introduces different variants for calculating the alignment scores."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Dot: e_ij = s_i^T * h_j"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"General: e_ij = s_i^T * W_a * h_j"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Concat: e_ij = v_a^T * tanh(W_a * [s_i; h_j])"},{"order":17,"type":"heading","text":"Key Differences: Bahdanau vs Luong"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Architecture: Bahdanau uses a bidirectional RNN encoder and aligns using the previous decoder state (s_{i-1}). Luong typically uses the current decoder state (s_i)."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Computation: Bahdanau is additive (uses a feed-forward network), whereas Luong relies more on multiplicative dot-products, making it computationally faster and more space-efficient."},{"order":20,"type":"heading","text":"Python Implementation Example (Conceptual Luong Dot Attention)"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

def luong_dot_attention(decoder_state, encoder_states):
    # decoder_state shape: (batch_size, hidden_dim)
    # encoder_states shape: (batch_size, seq_len, hidden_dim)
    
    # Calculate scores (dot product)
    scores = torch.bmm(encoder_states, decoder_state.unsqueeze(2)).squeeze(2)
    
    # Calculate attention weights
    attention_weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=1)
    
    # Calculate context vector
    context_vector = torch.bmm(attention_weights.unsqueeze(1), encoder_states).squeeze(1)
    
    return context_vector, attention_weights"},{"order":22,"type":"heading","text":"Summary"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"Both Bahdanau and Luong attention laid the critical foundation for modern Transformer architectures. While RNN-based attention models are largely succeeded by self-attention mechanisms in Transformers, understanding these foundational concepts is essential for deep learning engineers in NLP."}]
